title: What does this evidence establish?
subtitle: Separate a recorded malfunction, a statutory presumption and a remedy condition.
summary: Separate a recorded malfunction, a statutory presumption and a remedy condition. Work through fictional evidence cards without calculating a personal entitlement.
audience: General readers; all selected evidence and task instructions are included.
scope: Reading exercise on selected Consumer Rights Act 2015 provisions for the stated England-and-Wales scenario. Section-specific editorial snapshots are retained; not a consolidated legal opinion.

passages.title: Locate the proposition
passages.text: Section 19(14) names routes in (3)(b), (c) and (4), with exceptions in (15). The presumption concerns conformity at delivery; it is not an unconditional six-month refund rule or an automatic extension to (3)(a).
passages.context: Original bounded summary of the dated source reading; see source scope and limits.

passages.title: Locate the remedy conditions
passages.text: Section 23 addresses repair or replacement, including impossibility, disproportion, reasonable time and significant inconvenience. These conditions need their own facts.
passages.context: Original bounded summary of the dated source reading; see source scope and limits.

passages.title: Request versus completion
passages.text: Section 24(5)–(7) distinguishes routes to price reduction or final rejection. Asking for a repair does not establish that a repair was completed.
passages.context: Original bounded summary of the dated source reading; see source scope and limits.

passages.title: Fictional file: a kettle
passages.text: Delivery record: 1 March. Video: the kettle does not switch on on 1 May. The video says nothing about the internal cause or condition on delivery. A repair was requested on 3 May. No completion record is present.
passages.context: Original fictional scenario; associated source supplies a method/context only, not these facts.

passages.title: Two additional fictional cards
passages.text: Card A: a report alleges a latent component fault but explains no test. Card B: a dated photograph shows later impact damage but does not establish whether it caused the malfunction. Both causes remain disputed.
passages.context: Original fictional scenario; associated source supplies a method/context only, not these facts.

claims.text: Separate the observed failure from its cause and delivery condition.
claims.qualification: Reading exercise on selected Consumer Rights Act 2015 provisions for the stated England-and-Wales scenario. Section-specific editorial snapshots are retained; not a consolidated legal opinion.

context: Sections 19, 23 and 24 were read again on 23 October; downloaded bodies match the retained hashes. Notices retain different known-change cutoffs; a common effective-date consolidation is not claimed.
No personal transactions, documents or litigation assessment are requested. The example is an original teaching file.

lenses.label: Identify the disputed proposition
lenses.observation: The May recording shows the stipulated malfunction; delivery condition and cause remain separate.
lenses.question: Which proposition does each card support?
readings: Build a row for the recorded failure, a row for delivery condition and a row for cause; locate each source.
Ask what inspection or provenance evidence would distinguish the competing explanations.
lenses.boundary: Do not assign a numerical probability of winning or invent an inspection result.

lenses.label: Read the route before using a presumption
lenses.observation: The named cross-references and exceptions limit the presumption.
lenses.question: Why is selecting a remedy route necessary before invoking s19(14)?
readings: Trace the actual cross-references and keep their exclusions visible.
Explain how contrary delivery/cause evidence would require further analysis instead of an automatic result.
lenses.boundary: Elapsed time alone does not establish a complete entitlement.

lenses.label: Find the missing event
lenses.observation: A request appears in the file but a completed repair does not.
lenses.question: What changes if a dated return-after-repair record is later supplied?
readings: It can supply evidence of an event missing from the current file.
It still does not automatically establish every condition of the chosen remedy.
lenses.boundary: No universal deadline or procedural advice is supplied.

activity.transfer: Write a three-column note: proposition, supporting evidence, unresolved question. Then identify the exact provision needed for one selected remedy route. Explain why the video alone is insufficient.
rubric: Separate the observed failure from its cause and delivery condition.
Read the presumption’s named routes and exceptions.
Keep remedy conditions separate from factual evidence.
Treat an unrecorded completion as unknown, not as a completed repair.
